subject: [AMBER] pmemd.cuda fails with "cudaMemcpyToSymbol: SetSim copy to cSim failed invalid device symbol"

messages.author: Laura SCALVINI
messages.body:
Dear Amber users,
I am installing Amber16 with AmberTools17 on a redhat 7 workstation with 2 NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3070. I have installed the Nvidia Driver version 460.73.01 and the Cuda toolkit 8.0 version 8.0.61. I can successfully install the pmemd.mpi and pmemd.cuda modules, but when I try to run a MD simulation on a minimized benchmark system (already tested on Amber16 running pmemd.cuda, with different GPU and NVIDIA drivers, but same Cuda toolkit) the simulation fails with the following error:
cudaMemcpyToSymbol: SetSim copy to cSim failed invalid device symbol
I am writing to ask if there are some inconsistencies between the cuda toolkit version/Amber version and the GPUs I have installed/NVIDIA drivers version, and if you can suggest any tip to overcome this issue.
Many thanks in advance for your time and help,
Best regards
Laura

messages.author: David A Case
messages.body:
On Mon, May 03, 2021, Laura SCALVINI wrote:
>
>I am installing Amber16 with AmberTools17 on a redhat 7 workstation with
>2 NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3070. I have installed the Nvidia Driver version
>460.73.01 and the Cuda toolkit 8.0 version 8.0.61.
>
>cudaMemcpyToSymbol: SetSim copy to cSim failed invalid device symbol
According to the Amber GPU Hardware page
(
https://ambermd.org/GPUHardware.php
), the RTX 3070 card requires at least
version 11 of the Cuda toolkit.  I'm also suspecting (others can chime in
here) that you will need to upgrade Amber itself as well, to version 20.
Support for CUDA 11 wasn't added until August of 2020.
....regards....dac
